1.word_for_word: ṣaṭ-triṃśe — in the thirty-sixth chapter; hate ariṣṭe — when Ariṣṭa had been killed; nārada-uktyā — through Nārada's statement; bala-acyutau vasudeva-sutau jñātvā — learning that Balarāma and Acyuta were Vasudeva's sons; kaṃsaḥ akrūram samādiśat — Kaṃsa instructed Akrūra; gopī-rāsa-antarāya-āntam śaṅkhacūḍam nihatya — after killing Śaṅkhacūḍa, who came as an obstacle to the gopīs' rāsa; gopī-mahānanda-saham duṣṭam ariṣṭakam ahan — he killed the wicked Ariṣṭa, together with the great joy of the gopīs; atha-śabdaḥ — the word atha; tad-viruddha-artha-antara-adhikāra-artham — introduces a contrary new subject; vṛṣabha-ākṛtiḥ asuraḥ — a demon in the form of a bull; mahāntau kakut-kāyau yasya — whose hump and body were huge; khuraiḥ vidāritām mahīm kampayan — shaking the earth torn by his hooves
1.translation: In the thirty-sixth chapter, after Ariṣṭa had been killed, Kaṃsa learned from Nārada that Balarāma and Acyuta were the sons of Vasudeva and instructed Akrūra. Having killed Śaṅkhacūḍa, who had come as an obstacle to the gopīs' rāsa, Kṛṣṇa then killed the wicked Ariṣṭa, whose coming had disturbed the gopīs' great joy. When Kṛṣṇa had returned and Vraja was in the midst of a supreme festival, with songs, dancing, music and showers of flowers from the gods, Gandharvas and others, the word ‘atha’ introduces a new subject of the opposite character. ‘Then’ means at that very time. The demon had the form of a bull. His description extends through three and a half verses: his hump and body were enormous, and he shook the earth that his hooves had torn open.

2.word_for_word: rambhamāṇaḥ — bellowing; vṛṣabha-jāti-śabdam kurvan — making the characteristic sound of a bull; vilikhan — tearing open; udyamya — raising upward; vaprāṇi taṭāni utkṣipan — throwing up embankments and banks
2.translation: ‘Bellowing’ means making the characteristic sound of a bull. ‘Scratching’ means tearing open. ‘Raising’ means lifting upward, and he was throwing up embankments and banks.

3.word_for_word: kiñcit kiñcit śakṛt — a little dung at a time; madhye madhye — from time to time; purīṣam muñcan — discharging feces; mūtrayan — urinating; mūtram utsṛjan — releasing urine; stabdha-locanaḥ — with fixed eyes; animiṣa-locanaḥ — unblinking-eyed; yasya dhvaninā — by whose sound; gavām nārīṇām ca — of the cows and women
3.translation: He discharged a little dung from time to time and also urinated. ‘With fixed eyes’ means that his eyes did not blink. By the sound he made, the cows and women were affected as described in the verse.

4.word_for_word: ā-caturthāt bhavet srāvaḥ — up to the fourth month it is called discharge or miscarriage; pātaḥ pañcama-ṣaṣṭhayoḥ — in the fifth and sixth, a fall or abortion; ata ūrdhvam prasūtiḥ syāt — beyond that it is called delivery; kakudi — on the hump; gala-pṛṣṭha-śṛṅge — the projection on the back of the neck
4.translation: The classification is: ‘Up to the fourth month it is termed a miscarriage; in the fifth and sixth months, an abortion; beyond that, a delivery.’ ‘Kakud’ here is the raised projection on the back of the neck, the hump.

5.word_for_word: tīkṣṇe śṛṅga-agre yasya — whose horn-tips were sharp; tam vīkṣya — seeing him
5.translation: They saw him with his sharply pointed horns.

6.word_for_word: kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa rakṣa iti — ‘Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Protect us!’
6.translation: Their cry was: ‘Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Protect us!’

8.word_for_word: iti evam vadan — speaking thus; āsphoṭya — slapping; kara-talena bāhum āhatya — striking his arm with his palm; tena tala-śabdena kopayan — provoking him by the sound of that slap
8.translation: Speaking in this way, Kṛṣṇa slapped his arm with the palm of his hand and provoked the demon with the sound of the slap.

9.word_for_word: bhujā-bhogam — the coil-like arm; bhujā eva bhogaḥ sarpa-dehaḥ — the arm itself compared with a serpent's coiled body; sarpa-deha-ākāram bhujam — an arm shaped like a serpent's body; acyutaḥ — Acyuta; anyān duṣṭān harati iti hariḥ — Hari because he removes other wicked beings; udyatā ūrdhvam gacchatā pucchena — by the tail raised upward; bhramantaḥ meghāḥ yasmin — around which the clouds seemed to whirl
9.translation: ‘His serpent-like arm’ means an arm whose form resembled the coiled body of a serpent. Acyuta is called Hari because he removes the wicked. With Ariṣṭa's tail raised high, the clouds appeared to whirl around it.

10.word_for_word: agre nyaste viṣāṇa-agre yena — with the tips of his horns thrust forward; stabdhe asṛk-tulye locane yasya — whose fixed eyes were like blood; kaṭākṣipya — casting a sidelong glance; kaṭākṣeṇa tiryak nirīkṣya — looking obliquely from the corner of the eye
10.translation: He advanced with the tips of his horns thrust forward, his fixed eyes blood-red. ‘Kaṭākṣipya’ means looking at Kṛṣṇa obliquely with a sidelong glance.

11.word_for_word: pratyapovāha — he drove him back; pratilomam vyanudat — he thrust him away in the opposite direction
11.translation: ‘He drove him back’ means that Kṛṣṇa thrust him away in the opposite direction.

12.word_for_word: apaviddhaḥ — hurled away; apakṣiptaḥ — thrown aside; āpatat — rushed forward; ādravat — charged; svinnāni — sweating; sveda-yuktāni sarvāṅgāni yasya — whose entire body was covered with sweat; krodha-mūrcchitaḥ — overcome by anger; krodhena vyāptaḥ — pervaded by rage
12.translation: ‘Hurled away’ means thrown aside. He then rushed and charged forward. His whole body was covered with sweat, and ‘overcome by anger’ means that rage had completely possessed him.

13.word_for_word: kṛtvā viṣāṇam utpāṭya — having seized and torn out the horn; tena eva jaghāna — struck him with that very horn; saḥ ca apatat — and he fell
13.translation: Kṛṣṇa tore out one of his horns and struck him with that very horn; then Ariṣṭa fell.

14.word_for_word: mūtram ca śakṛt ca mūtra-śakṛt — urine and feces, expressed as a compound; tad-ubhayam samutsṛjan — discharging both; pādān kṣipan — throwing his legs; itaḥ tataḥ cālayan — moving them this way and that; anavasthita-īkṣaṇaḥ — with unsteady eyes; pracalita-netraḥ — eyes rolling about; kṛcchram jagāma — came to distress; nirṛteḥ mṛtyoḥ kṣayam — the abode of Nirṛti, death; kṛcchram yathā bhavati tathā mṛtaḥ iti vā — alternatively, he died painfully
14.translation: ‘Mūtra-śakṛt’ combines urine and feces, meaning that he discharged both. He flung his legs about in every direction, and ‘with unsteady eyes’ means that his eyes rolled. He came to great distress and then went to the abode of Nirṛti, that is, death. Alternatively, the phrase means simply that he died painfully.

15.word_for_word: nayana-utsavaḥ — a festival for the eyes; nayanānām mūrtimān utsavaḥ — a festival for the eyes embodied in visible form
15.translation: ‘A festival for the eyes’ means a festival for the eyes embodied in visible form.

16.word_for_word: kāmam vraje vasantam tam kṛṣṇam — although Kṛṣṇa was dwelling in Vraja; tena tu vismṛtam — he had nevertheless been forgotten by him; nāradaḥ smārayām āsa kaṃsam — Nārada reminded Kaṃsa; dūta-gīḥ eva tu — merely through the words of a messenger; devadarśanaḥ devarṣiḥ — the divine seer, the devarṣi; yad vā — alternatively; sākṣāt deva-vat darśanam jñānam yasya — one whose knowledge sees directly like a god
16.translation: Although Kṛṣṇa was dwelling in Vraja, Kaṃsa had for the moment lost sight of him; Nārada reminded Kaṃsa merely by delivering his message. ‘Deva-darśana,’ referring to the devarṣi, may mean ‘one who has divine vision’; alternatively, one whose knowledge directly sees how events will unfold, as though with the vision of a god.

17.word_for_word: āptena iva nāradena uktam — what was stated by Nārada as by a trustworthy authority; devakyā aṣṭama-garbhatvena prasiddhām kanyām — the girl known as Devakī's eighth pregnancy; yaśodāyāḥ sutām āha — he identifies as Yaśodā's daughter; yaśodā-sutatvena prasiddham kṛṣṇam — Kṛṣṇa, known as Yaśodā's son; devakyāḥ sutam āha — he identifies as Devakī's son; rohiṇī-putram rāmam — Rāma, Rohiṇī's son; devakyāḥ saptamam sutam āha — he identifies as Devakī's seventh son; yad vā — alternatively; nanda-sutatvena prasiddham rāmam — Rāma known as Nanda's son; vasudeva-bhāryāyā rohiṇyāḥ putram āha — he identifies as the son of Rohiṇī, Vasudeva's wife; tau vasudeva-sutau cet katham vrajam gatau — if the two were Vasudeva's sons, how did they reach Vraja?; vasudevena iti — this is answered by ‘by Vasudeva’
17.translation: Nārada speaks as a trustworthy authority in the verse beginning ‘Yaśodā's.’ He identifies the girl commonly regarded as Devakī's eighth child as Yaśodā's daughter; Kṛṣṇa, commonly regarded as Yaśodā's son, as Devakī's son; and Rāma, Rohiṇī's son, as Devakī's seventh child. Alternatively, he identifies Rāma, commonly regarded as Nanda's son, as the son of Rohiṇī, Vasudeva's wife. If these two were Vasudeva's sons, how did they come to Vraja? The verse answers this with the words ‘by Vasudeva.’

19.word_for_word: nivāritaḥ iti — ‘was restrained’; hate vasudeve tau palāyetām — if Vasudeva were killed, the two boys might flee; ataḥ badhyatām — therefore let him be bound; iti mantram vadatā nāradena nivāritaḥ — Nārada restrained him by giving this counsel
19.translation: ‘He was restrained’ means that Nārada stopped Kaṃsa with the counsel: ‘If Vasudeva is killed, the two boys may flee; therefore Vasudeva should instead be bound.’

23.word_for_word: mahyam mama — to me, for me; nidarśitaḥ — pointed out, indicated; vidhātrā nāradena vā — by the Creator, or by Nārada
23.translation: ‘Indicated to me’ means pointed out for me by destiny—the Creator—or by Nārada.

24.word_for_word: vrajam gantum udyatau — ready to go to Vraja; tau āha — he addressed the two; bhavadbhyām iti — with the words ‘by you two’; mañcāḥ — platforms; uttuṅga-stambha-abhiracita-sthānāni — places constructed on lofty pillars
24.translation: As the two were preparing to go to Vraja, Kaṃsa addressed them with the words ‘by you two.’ ‘Mañcas’ are platforms or raised places constructed upon lofty pillars.

26.word_for_word: mīḍhuṣe — to the bestower; varadāya — to the giver of boons

27.word_for_word: artha-tantra-jñaḥ — one who knows the practical means to an end; artha-siddhāntam eva jānāti — knows precisely the conclusion by which the objective is accomplished
27.translation: An ‘artha-tantra-jña’ is one who understands the practical means to an end—one who knows precisely the course by which the objective is accomplished.

28.word_for_word: he dāna-pate akrūra — O Akrūra, lord of generosity; maitram mitra-kṛtyam — a friendly service, the duty of a friend; tvayā kriyatām — let it be done by you; tvattaḥ anyaḥ ādṛtaḥ sādaraḥ hita-tamaḥ ca na vidyate — there is no one other than you more respected, attentive or beneficial to me
28.translation: ‘O Akrūra, lord of generosity, perform this friendly service for me. I have no one besides you whom I esteem more, who is more attentive to me, or who is more useful to my purpose.’

29.word_for_word: tau me mṛtyuḥ nitarām sṛṣṭaḥ — those two have been specifically produced as my death; vaikuṇṭha-saṃśrayaiḥ — by those sheltered in Vaikuṇṭha; viṣṇu-saṃśrayaiḥ devaiḥ — by the gods who take shelter of Viṣṇu
29.translation: ‘Those two have been deliberately brought forth as my death by the gods who take shelter of Viṣṇu, the residents dependent upon Vaikuṇṭha.’

31.word_for_word: tau me mṛtyuḥ nitarām sṛṣṭaḥ — those two have been specifically produced as my death; vaikuṇṭha-saṃśrayaiḥ — by those sheltered in Vaikuṇṭha; viṣṇu-saṃśrayaiḥ devaiḥ — by the gods who take shelter of Viṣṇu
31.translation: The sense is again: ‘Those two have been deliberately produced as my death by the gods who have taken shelter of Viṣṇu.’

32.word_for_word: kim tataḥ — what then?; tatra āha ghātayiṣye iti — to this he says, ‘I shall have them killed’; kāla-kalpena — comparable to Time, death; mṛtyu-tulyena — equal to death; vaidyuta-upamaiḥ — like lightning; aśani-tulyaiḥ — like thunderbolts
32.translation: What will happen then? Kaṃsa answers with ‘I shall have them killed.’ The expressions describe forces comparable to Time or death and like lightning or thunderbolts.

35.word_for_word: naṣṭa-kaṇṭakā — with the thorns removed; naṣṭa-śatruḥ — with enemies destroyed; katipaya-asuhṛd-vadhena — by killing only a few enemies; katham syāt — how would that be achieved?; jarāsandha iti — this is answered by the reference to Jarāsandha
35.translation: ‘With the thorns removed’ means ‘with the enemies destroyed.’ One may ask: how could all opposition be removed merely by killing a few enemies? The verse answers this by mentioning Jarāsandha and the others.

37.word_for_word: yadu-pura-śriyam — the splendor of the city of the Yadus; draṣṭum ca — and to behold
37.translation: The phrase also means ‘in order to behold the splendor of the city of the Yadus.’

38.word_for_word: sva-manīṣitam — what he had himself considered; vicāritam — thought out; sadhryak — properly, correctly; sva-avadyaṃ maraṇam — his own blameworthy death or ruin; tat-mārjanam — its removal; etāvān abhiniveśaḥ na kāryaḥ — such excessive fixation should nevertheless not be maintained; siddhi-asiddhyoḥ iti — this future point is indicated by ‘in success and failure’
38.translation: He had properly considered his own plan: how to remove the danger of his own death. Yet the text also indicates, by the coming statement about success and failure, that one should not become excessively fixated even upon a carefully devised plan.

39.word_for_word: puruṣa-kārasya vyabhicāram — the possibility that human effort may fail or deviate from its intended result; mano-rathān iti — expressed by the words concerning mental plans
39.translation: The words concerning one's plans show that human effort is not infallible and may fail to produce its intended result.
